kept.excerpt: Mark Sutcliffe had 53% support among decided voters, compared with 31% for Jeff Leiper, 8% for Neil Saravanamuttoo and 7% for Alex Lawson; 23% of all voters remained undecided. Sutcliffe led in Ottawa's west, east and rural areas, while Leiper led downtown. The survey interviewed 762 adult Ottawa residents from October 4–8, 2026, using a hybrid random telephone and online methodology, with a reported margin of error of ±3.6 percentage points, 19 times out of 20.
kept.relevance: This is a recent primary-source voting-intention poll available before the cutoff, identifying Sutcliffe's lead, his principal challenger and the remaining undecided electorate.

kept.excerpt: Ottawa residents were more likely to say the city was going in the right direction (34%) than the wrong direction (15%), while 48% were neutral. Residents gave mixed reviews of City Hall's performance in listening to citizens.
kept.relevance: The city's direction and City Hall's responsiveness provide contemporaneous context for assessing the incumbent's electoral position.

kept.excerpt: A majority of Ottawa residents cited transit as the top priority for improvement, with better LRT service and more reliable buses among the leading solutions. The findings came from a survey of 762 adult Ottawa residents conducted October 4–8, 2026.
kept.relevance: This identifies a leading campaign issue on which voters could evaluate Sutcliffe and his challengers; it comes from the same survey as the October 9 voting-intention release.

kept.excerpt: Advance Voting Day for the 2026 Municipal Elections will take place on Friday, October 16, with voting at assigned ward locations from 10 am to 8 pm. Completed Special Ballot Voter Kits must be received by 8 pm that day to be counted. Electors who do not vote on Advance Voting Day will have one additional in-person opportunity on Voting Day, Monday, October 26.
kept.relevance: This dated official notice confirms the election schedule and the voting opportunities still ahead as of October 13.

kept.excerpt: An ElectRight poll conducted September 17–18 found 35% support for Sutcliffe, 19% for Jeff Leiper, 10% for Neil Saravanamuttoo and 4% for Alex Lawson, while 28% were unsure. Commissioned by Ottawa Compass and iPolitics, the poll surveyed roughly 600 people by phone and text messages and reported a margin of error of ±4 percentage points.
kept.relevance: This supplies an earlier poll from a different polling organization, although its all-respondent percentages should not be directly compared with Nanos's decided-voter percentages.

kept.excerpt: With municipal nominations closed, 14 candidates were vying for mayor, including incumbent Mark Sutcliffe, who was seeking a second term. The listed mayoral candidates included Jeff Leiper, Alex Lawson and Neil Saravanamuttoo. The municipal election was scheduled for October 26.
kept.relevance: This establishes Sutcliffe's candidacy, incumbency and the contested mayoral field following the close of nominations.

search_notes: Frozen evidence cutoff: 2026-10-13, inclusive, for Q090. All included items have explicit publication dates on or before the cutoff verified in web_search's indexed source text. Excerpts are factual paraphrases. Post-cutoff material, election outcomes, prediction-market pages and betting prices were excluded. Direct web_fetch failed because of a provider-configuration error; the requested agent-reach web-read fallback returned RATE_LIMITED, so verification relied on indexed source content rather than successful direct page retrieval. The three Nanos releases draw on the same October 4–8 survey and should not be treated as independent polls. Live URLs are supplied for provenance; immutable archived copies were not obtained.
